chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is a certain hour in the night; if a Muslim servant coincides with it, then prays and supplicates to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in it, He will answer him. I said: May Allah keep you well! And which hour of the night is it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When half the night has passed, and it is the first sixth from the beginning of the half.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific time in the night when prayers are most likely to be answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the 'first sixth of the second half' of the night as a prime window for divine acceptance, a period traditionally associated with the Tahajjud prayer and spiritual tranquility. This specific timing underscores the Shia emphasis on nocturnal devotion as a means to draw closer to Allah when the world is asleep, reflecting the concept of *Istijabah* (answering) for the sincere supplicant.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘During the night there is a particular time in which no Muslim servant would be harmonious with it, then prays Salāt and supplicates to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic therein except that it would be Answered for him during every night’. I said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! And which time it is from the night?’ Heasws said: ‘When half the night passes by, and it is the first sixth from the first half’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘In a night there is an hour during which if a Muslim servant (of Allah) has the opportunity to perform a formal prayer and then plead before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, for help, he will receive an answer every night.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘May Allah grant you well being, which hour of night is that?’ The Imam said, ‘It is the first one-sixth of the second half of the night.’”
